seoDescription: Hurt at work in Warren, at a plant, the Tech Center, a supplier shop, or the Arsenal? Michigan workers’ comp owes you 80 percent of your after-tax wage and all medical care. The benefits, the 90-day notice, the 28-day doctor rule, staffing-agency workers, federal employees, and the third-party suit comp does not bar. Free review. (313) 406-7606.
tagline: The automakers insure themselves and run injured workers’ claims through their own plant medical departments; the supplier shops often staff their lines through agencies; the civilian workforce at the Arsenal is under a different, federal system. The Act gives you 80 percent of your after-tax wage, every medical bill, and a hearing. It also gives you 90 days to report the injury.

c.v: A worker hurt on the job in Warren is owed benefits under Michigan’s Workers’ Disability Compensation Act regardless of fault: medical care in full, 80 percent of after-tax wages while unable to work, vocational rehabilitation, and scheduled payments for the loss of a body part. What differs in Warren is who is on the other side. General Motors at the Technical Center and Stellantis at Warren Truck Assembly and Warren Stamping are self-insured and administer claims through their own adjusters and plant medical departments. The supplier, tool-and-die, and logistics shops along Mound, Van Dyke, Groesbeck, and Stephens are smaller employers, many of which staff their lines through temporary agencies. And civilian employees at the Detroit Arsenal are not under Michigan’s Act at all.

sections.heading: Where Warren workers are hurt, and who handles the claim

c.v: Repetitive-motion injuries to shoulders, wrists, and backs; crush and amputation injuries from presses, robotics, and conveyors; forklift strikes; falls; and burns. The automakers are self-insured, and the first 28 days of care are typically at plant medical. Union contracts add grievance rights and sickness-and-accident benefits that interact with comp (MCL 418.354).
The Tech Center and engineering campuses.

Engineering, design, and test work: vehicle-testing and shop injuries, falls on icy lots and stairs, and repetitive strain. Contractors’ and vendors’ employees on the campus are covered by their own employer’s comp, and the campus owner can be a third-party defendant; see our

Tool-and-die, machining, plating, and logistics operations, where a large share of the workforce may be placed by a staffing agency. A placed worker is the agency’s employee for comp, and the host plant may also be protected by the exclusive-remedy bar under Michigan’s economic-reality test, which affects whether the plant can be sued as a third party. Some small shops carry no workers’ compensation insurance. An uninsured employer loses the exclusive-remedy protection: the worker may claim comp benefits and may also sue the employer in circuit court, and officers can be personally liable (MCL 418.641, 418.647).

Civilian federal employees at the Arsenal are covered by the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act, administered by the U.S. Department of Labor, not by Michigan’s Act: written notice on Form CA-1 or CA-2 within 30 days, a claim within three years, and no lawsuit against the United States for the injury (5 USC 8101 et seq.). Employees of private defense contractors on the base are under Michigan’s Act through their own employer.

Warren Police, Fire, and Public Works; the school districts serving the city; and Henry Ford Warren Hospital: public-safety injuries, patient-handling injuries, and assaults. Public employers have pension and duty-disability provisions that run alongside comp, and police officers and firefighters have a statutory presumption for certain heart and respiratory conditions (MCL 418.405).

sections.heading: The hearing, and the lawsuit comp does not bar

c.v: When an employer or insurer denies a claim or stops paying, the worker files an Application for Mediation or Hearing (Form WC-104A) with the Workers’ Disability Compensation Agency. Disputed claims go to mediation and then to a magistrate, with appeal to the Michigan Compensation Appellate Commission. Macomb County claims are heard at the agency’s Detroit hearing site at Cadillac Place, 3026 W. Grand Boulevard, Suite 3-700. A contested claim often takes a year or more, which is why many disputed claims resolve by
, a lump-sum settlement approved by the magistrate that closes the claim, including future medical care (MCL 418.835). Do not sign one without advice.

Workers’ compensation is your exclusive remedy against an insured employer (MCL 418.131), with one narrow exception: an employer that specifically intended an injury, meaning it had actual knowledge that an injury was certain to occur and willfully disregarded that knowledge (MCL 418.131(1)). faqs.question: How long do I have to report a work injury in Warren?

answer.v: Ninety days from the injury, or from when you knew it was work-related, to notify your employer, and two years to file a claim. Report it in writing the day it happens.

faqs.question: I was hurt at a plant. Is plant medical my only option?

answer.v: For the first 28 days, generally yes. After that you may treat with your own physician on written notice. Your union contract may also provide sickness-and-accident benefits and grievance rights that run alongside the comp claim.

faqs.question: I was placed at the plant by a staffing agency. Who pays my comp?

answer.v: Usually the staffing agency’s insurer. Whether you can also sue the plant depends on how much control it had over your work; if it counts as your employer too, comp is your only remedy against it.

faqs.question: I work at the Arsenal. Does Michigan workers’ comp apply?

answer.v: Not if you are a federal civilian employee. Your claim is under the Federal Employees’ Compensation Act, with notice within 30 days. If you work for a private contractor on the base, Michigan’s Act applies through your employer.

Not if it is insured, except in the narrow case where it knew an injury was certain to occur and willfully disregarded that. You can sue any other company or person whose negligence caused the injury, including the maker of a defective machine, and an uninsured employer directly.

faqs.question: I was in a crash on I-696 while driving for work. Who pays?

answer.v: Workers’ compensation pays your medical and wage-loss benefits first, your no-fault insurer pays what comp does not cover, and the at-fault driver is liable for pain and suffering if you have a threshold injury.

faqs.question: What does a Warren workers’ comp lawyer cost?

answer.v: Nothing up front. Fees are limited by state rule to a percentage of the benefits recovered and must be approved by the magistrate. You owe nothing if no benefits are recovered.
